title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction
slides: Can Dream's AI world models rebuild construction?
Dream simulates entire builds before ground is broken
Contractors must now treat AI models as planning tools
Test one project this quarter against a simulated build
thread_text:
1. AI That Builds Before You Do

Dream's AI simulates entire construction projects before ground is broken, and it just raised $17M from a16z. The founders are ex-Palantir execs who think world models can rebuild the industry.

2. From Defense To Construction

Palantir alumni are applying military-grade simulation to building sites. Their startup, Dream, uses AI to model every step of a project, catching errors before they become expensive.

3. Test Drive Your Build

Contractors are now using AI models as planning tools, not just fancy visualizations. Dream's simulation lets you test scenarios and optimize schedules without risking real-world delays.

4. The End Of Guesswork

With Dream, you can simulate an entire build and see the outcome before committing resources. That means fewer surprises, tighter budgets, and faster timelines.

5. Ready To Simulate?

Pick one upcoming project and run it through a simulated build this quarter. If you haven't tried AI planning yet, start with a small test case and measure the difference.
video_script: What if you could build something twice—first in AI, then in reality?
Dream, founded by ex-Palantir execs, just raised $17 million to do exactly that.
Their AI simulates entire construction projects before ground is broken.
Contractors can now test scenarios and catch errors early, saving time and money.
Try it on one project this quarter and see the impact.
